e.etymology: Italian and Spanish form of the Roman name Lucius, from Latin lux, 'light'. Lucius was one of the commonest first names in ancient Rome.

assoc.t: Lucio, the skating DJ hero in Overwatch

e.etymology: A modern spelling in the family of Cael and Kale. Cael is an Irish name from caol, 'slender'; the Kael spelling has also been a favorite of fantasy novels and games.
e.note: Sounds the same as kale, the leafy green.

e.etymology: A short form of Eliza and Elizabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, 'my God is an oath'. In Russian it is the everyday short form of Yelizaveta.
From an English surname of uncertain origin, possibly a variant of Brierley. As a girls' name it blends the sounds of Bailey, Riley and Brynlee.
A spelling of Austin, the medieval English contraction of Augustine, from Latin augustus, 'majestic, venerable'. This spelling recalls the novelist Jane Austen.

assoc.t: Jane Austen, author of Pride and Prejudice (surname)

e.etymology: From Hawaiian noe, 'mist', and lani, 'sky, heaven'. A longer related name is Kanoelani.
A feminine spelling of Vivian, from the Latin name Vivianus, from vivus, 'alive'. Tennyson used Vivien for the enchantress who ensnares Merlin, and Vivien Leigh made the spelling famous.
namesakes: Vivien Leigh (Scarlett O'Hara in Gone with the Wind)

assoc.t: Vivien Leigh, Scarlett O'Hara in Gone with the Wind

e.etymology: A modern American coinage joining Ray with the -len ending of Jalen and Braylen. The spelling Raylan became familiar through Raylan Givens, the marshal of the TV series Justified.
From an English surname that began as a place name. As a girls' name it follows the fashion for surnames ending in -ley, such as Hadley and Henley.
A recent spelling with no single source. It may be read as a variant of Zion, as Ryan with a Z, or as a form of Zayan, an Arabic name related to Zayn, 'beauty'.
From Old Norse valkyrja, 'chooser of the slain': valr, 'the slain', plus a form of kjosa, 'to choose'. In Norse myth the valkyries are Odin's maidens who carry fallen warriors to Valhalla.

assoc.t: valkyries, Odin's warrior maidens in Norse myth
Valkyrie, Asgardian warrior in Marvel's Thor films
Operation Valkyrie, the 1944 plot to kill Hitler

e.etymology: A spelling of Giselle favored by Spanish-speaking families. Giselle is the French form of a Germanic name from gisil, 'pledge', and the title of a famous 1841 ballet.
Spanish form of Christopher, from Greek Christophoros, 'bearing Christ'. Cristobal Colon is the Spanish name of Christopher Columbus.

assoc.t: Cristobal, a recurring Atlantic tropical storm name

e.etymology: A respelling of Briar, the English word for a thorny shrub such as the wild rose. Briar Rose is the name of Sleeping Beauty in the Grimm tale.
From the Arabic command iqra, 'read' or 'recite', held to be the first word of the Quran revealed to Muhammad. As a girls' name it is most common in Pakistan.
A spelling of Arlette, the French form of Herleva, the name of William the Conqueror's mother. Arlett, Arleth and Arlet are widely used by Spanish-speaking families in the US.
A medieval English pet form of Eleanor, Ellen and Helen. The N came from the phrase 'mine Ell', which was heard as 'my Nell'.
namesakes: Nell Carter (singer and star of Gimme a Break!)
Little Nell (heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop)

e.etymology: A name used by Mexican and Mexican American families, built on the Kar- of Karla and Karen with the -ely ending of Arely and Nayeli. No older source is established.
From Old Norse Loki, the shape-shifting trickster god of Norse myth; the origin of the name itself is debated. American use rose with Tom Hiddleston's Loki in the Marvel films and series.

assoc.t: Loki, Marvel's god of mischief, played by Tom Hiddleston
Loki, trickster god of Norse mythology

e.note: Tied to a trickster god and Marvel antihero, and very common as a name for dogs and cats.

e.meaning: God is gracious (from Shawn, a form of John)
e.etymology: An African American coinage that adds the prefix De-, as in DeAndre and DeAngelo, to Shawn, the Irish form of John. It peaked in the 1990s.
From Arabic isra, 'night journey', the name of the Prophet Muhammad's journey from Mecca to Jerusalem and of a chapter of the Quran. In Spanish, Isra is separately a boys' short form of Israel.
The Swedish, Slovak, Croatian and Serbian form of Katherine, from Greek Aikaterine. The original meaning is uncertain; early Christians linked it to katharos, 'pure'.
namesakes: Katarina Witt (German Olympic figure skating champion)

assoc.t: Katarina, assassin champion in League of Legends

e.etymology: From a surname meaning 'son of Kendrick', an old given name with Welsh and Old English sources. It suits the recent taste for names ending in x, like Hendrix and Maddox.
From the name of the continent, Greek Asia, which first meant western Anatolia and probably comes from a Hittite place name. In Polish, Asia is separately a pet form of Joanna.

assoc.t: Asia, 1980s rock band behind Heat of the Moment

e.etymology: A modern American name, an elaboration of Jane or Janae with the -iya ending heard in Aniya and Shaniya. Through Jane it goes back to the Hebrew name meaning 'God is gracious'.

e.meaning: Ya-Sin, the 36th chapter of the Quran
e.etymology: From the Arabic letters ya and sin, the 'mysterious letters' that open and name the 36th chapter of the Quran. Tradition treats Yasin as one of the names of the Prophet Muhammad.

A name with several sources: Basque Naia, said to mean 'wave, sea foam'; Hawaiian nai'a, 'dolphin'; and in Danish a spelling of Naja, a name from Greenland. It also recalls the naiads, the water nymphs of Greek myth.
A spelling of Yasmin common among Spanish-speaking families. Yasmin is the Persian and Arabic name of the jasmine flower and the source of English Jasmine.
From the Sahara, the great desert of North Africa, whose name is Arabic sahra, 'desert'. As a given name it is a modern choice, close in sound to Sarah and Zahara.

assoc.t: the Sahara, the vast desert of North Africa
Sahara Las Vegas, hotel and casino on the Strip

e.etymology: A modern American name patterned on Mariah and Zariah with an initial N. It resembles the biblical Neriah, 'the Lord is my lamp', but no direct link is established.
From Sanskrit adya, 'first, original'. Adya Shakti, 'the primordial power', is a title of the goddess Durga.

e.meaning: truce, an agreement to stop fighting
e.etymology: From the English word for a halt in fighting, which goes back to Old English treow, 'faith, pledge', the root of true and trust. Its use as a first name is very recent.

assoc.t: truce, the ordinary word for a halt in fighting
